findings.title: A picture picked in H83's grid is reset by pinItemIcons, whose own header says a picture a GM picked is left alone
findings.where: scripts/inventory.mjs:451-457 replaceableIcon (any path under /icons/item- is the module's), :472-475 (the header: 'an item a GM picked art for, is left alone'), :497 (the skip); scripts/tables-editor.mjs:848 wireItemPicture
findings.what_happens: The grid stores one of the module's own item drawings in the item's img. pinItemIcons treats every module drawing as its own placeholder, so with apply it replaces the GM's pick with the category's drawing. The notes say so (v1.2.86.md:133-134); the function's header was not changed and still promises the GM's pick is kept.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM picks the knife drawing for a usable item in Create an item, later runs game.drpg.pinItemIcons({ apply: true }) to fix old items, and the item comes back with the usable category's drawing although the console help said chosen art is left alone.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a mark the grid leaves that pinItemIcons reads (none: the grid writes img alone) and for a later stage that changed replaceableIcon (none; the SUPERSEDED set and the /icons/item- test are as described). The behaviour is a stated known gap; what remains is the header's sentence against the code.

stages.what: Two parts, with E18's last commit (C7) in the same train. Part 1: one queue on the primary GM (Despair, search tokens, the clock, the overflow, the Eclipse's count, a tunnel's price, the trial's seizures, a project's row, each under its own key), the primary GM's put-back of a player's move into a room the rules shut and the delete of a refused sidebar drop, the Eclipse counted on the primary, Refund last crossing, a late search token's return, Despair's one writer. Part 2: the HUD's minutes played, no Eclipse over a running incident and the chevron's question, a boundary refilled once and taken back within five minutes, the motive due in an incident, the player's strip and room tile, a rest per chapter, the fog's dissolve, the Mastermind and public projects. E18 C7: a Frisk's ask ends with its wait, a Sabotage sent again answers its first result - 16 registry rows stamped E17 (R1006 is E18 C7's).

findings.title: A proposer knows their public project only while the GM's private card is in the chat: a cleared chat takes it off their tray and map, and nothing tells them again
findings.where: scripts/projects.mjs:338-343 proposedBy (a player's browser reads projectsToldHere), :641-650 projectsToldHere (game.messages, cards a GM wrote with PROJECT_KNOWN), :1963-1965 (toldHere forgotten on deleteChatMessage); :683-685 tellProposers skips a project marked proposerTold; :2143 (proposerTold set at approval)
findings.what_happens: On a player's browser proposedBy answers from the private card alone; the GMs' row holds who proposed but marks proposerTold at the approval, so the load's catch-up never posts again. When the chat no longer holds that card - a GM's Clear Chat Log, or the card deleted - the next read (the hook's forget, or a reload) finds no card, and the proposer knows the project only by the room rule, as anybody else. secret.mjs askForWords gives a card's words again, not a card that is gone.
findings.failure_scenario: A player proposes a public project; the GM approves it in the Library, where the player's character has never stood; the player sees it on their tray. At the end of the session the GM clears the chat log. Next session the project is gone from the proposer's tray and map although the handbook says the proposer sees it 'from the moment you approve it, wherever you put it' (gm-handbook.en.md:984).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a second road on the proposer's browser: the public meta holds no proposer since fix G3 (sealedViewers only for a sealed project), the discovery record covers only rooms stood in, knowsWithoutRoom reads the same proposedBy. Looked for a repost: tellProposers skips every row with proposerTold, which approval sets (:2143). Looked for a module road that deletes chat: season-wipe.mjs:382 (the season reset, which also ends projects) - so the ordinary road is Foundry's own Clear Chat. Not run: whether Foundry 14.370's Clear Chat fires deleteChatMessage on each browser does not matter, since a reload reads game.messages afresh. The notes name the card as the carrier and the away browser's case (Known gaps 147-150), not the card's loss.
findings.expected: The proposer's knowing a public project held in something that outlives the chat (a player copy of the GMs' row, or the card posted again when it is missing)

l1.what: Whether a proposer keeps their public project after the chat is cleared
recipe: One GM, one player; the player's character stands in Dorm A and has never stood in the Library
The player proposes a public project; the GM approves it with room Library
Read the player's Projects tray and the map: the project shows
The GM presses Foundry's Clear Chat Log
The player reloads; read the tray and the map again
